headline: GOLD TOUCHES 2026 YEAR LOW: Spot Hits $3,850 Intraday as CPI-Driven Rate-Hike Bets Crush Thursday's Recovery — Silver Flat at $50
snippet: Gold pierced its lowest level of 2026 at approximately $3,850 per ounce on November 13, erasing the early morning recovery above $3,900 and extending gold's correction from its January record. The move follows the hot October CPI print that reignited December Fed rate-hike pricing, with silver broadly unchanged near $50 — down roughly 29% from its year-to-date highs — as the monetary metals face the same macro headwind simultaneously.

headline: CODELCO + ADANI SIGN KABURKAALA COPPER MOU AT LME WEEK — India's Mundra Smelter Seeks Chilean Concentrate to Break China Dependency
snippet: Adani's Kutch Copper and Chile's state copper giant Codelco signed an MoU at LME Week London on November 11 to jointly explore the Kaburkaala copper project in Chile's Calama district, with the stated goal of securing long-term concentrate supply for Adani's Mundra smelter in Gujarat. The arrangement follows a 2025 concentrate supply pact between the same parties, expanding the relationship from supply contract to upstream exploration and potentially positioning Adani as a vertically integrated copper player with a Chilean resource base.

headline: PHYSICAL PRECIOUS METALS RALLY FIVE SESSIONS STRAIGHT — US Shutdown Resolution Drives Demand as Paper Gold Futures Hit Year Lows
snippet: Physical precious metals demand extended a five-session positive streak through November 13 as the resolution of the U.S. government shutdown drove buyers to bullion even as paper gold futures touched 2026 year lows. The divergence between weakening gold futures (driven by rate-hike repricing) and sustained physical buying represents a classic 'paper vs. physical' split that experienced gold investors monitor as a potential floor indicator — when physical demand holds up under futures-driven selling pressure, it typically signals institutional de-risking rather than a structural bearish reversal.

headline: 30-DAY COMMODITY SCOREBOARD: Lithium -14.7%, Copper -7.2% (But +21.85% YTD), Gold and Silver Near 52-Week Lows — Uranium Holds $90.55
snippet: A November 13 30-day commodity performance check shows lithium as the worst performer at -14.7%, with Chinese battery-grade lithium carbonate at CNY 92,350/t, while copper fell 7.2% over the period to approximately $6.14/lb but remains 21.85% above a year ago — context that separates the current correction from a trend reversal. Gold and silver are hovering near 52-week lows, while uranium held at US$90.55/lb (+0.61%), continuing to demonstrate relative resilience versus the broader precious metals correction.

headline: CAN USA RARE EARTH JUMP 10X? Motley Fool Maps the Bull Case After Q3 Revenue Miss — $3.1B Market Cap vs $3M Quarterly Sales
snippet: Motley Fool's November 12 analysis asks whether USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) — trading at $8.35 with a $3.1 billion market cap after its 11% post-earnings collapse — can reach 10x its current price, noting the stock sits 75% below its $32.80 52-week high while Serra Verde's first magnet shipments to the Pentagon are underway. The piece frames the debate between the structural bull case (Western magnet supply chain critical to defense, first-mover advantage) and the near-term risk (Q3 revenue of $3M vs. $14M consensus, profitability runway unclear given current rare earth oxide pricing).

headline: FIREFLY METALS HITS ~10% COPPER OVER 16 METRES AT GREEN BAY NEWFOUNDLAND — High-Grade Extends District-Scale System
snippet: FireFly Metals (ASX:FFM/TSX:FFM) reported high-grade copper drill results from its Green Bay project in Newfoundland this week, including intersections of approximately 16 metres at nearly 10% copper — a grade level that ranks among the highest disclosed from any active Canadian copper exploration programme in 2026. The results continue to extend the mineralised system within the prolific Green Bay copper-zinc belt, reinforcing FireFly's position as one of the most closely watched copper exploration stories on both the ASX and TSX.

headline: SILVER'S 6TH CONSECUTIVE ANNUAL SUPPLY DEFICIT: 46.3M OZ SHORTFALL — Yet Price Near $50 Reflects Little of the Structural Tightness
snippet: Silver is heading for its sixth consecutive year of physical market deficit at approximately 46.3 million ounces annually, with demand for solar panels, electronics and electric vehicles consistently outstripping mine production — yet the price has not repriced to reflect this structural tightness, trading around $50 per ounce. Shanghai Metals Market's analysis frames the disconnect as driven by financial market selling pressure from rate-hike expectations overwhelming physical scarcity signals, and poses the question retail silver investors are wrestling with: when will the structural deficit translate into a durable price floor?

headline: AGC EVERGREEN DRILL: 16m AT 2.3g/t Au, 12.2% Pb+Zn — Australian Gold and Copper Delivers Multi-Metal Hit in NSW
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) reported that RC hole EGRC018 at its Evergreen project intersected 16 metres at 2.3g/t gold, 70g/t silver, 1.4% copper, and 12.2% lead-zinc combined from 112 metres depth — a poly-metallic result that strengthens the project's economic case by stacking multiple revenue streams into a single mineralised interval. The result highlights how base metal credits in a gold-silver system can materially improve the economics of junior exploration projects operating in the current high-cost environment.

headline: ADANI-CODELCO COPPER MOU IS 'AN OPTION, NOT SUPPLY SECURITY' — Why India's Smelter Needs More Than an Exploration Pact
snippet: Discovery Alert's critical analysis of the Adani-Kutch Copper / Codelco MoU signed at LME Week argues the exploration partnership — covering the undeveloped Kaburkaala project in Chile's Calama district — represents a medium-term sourcing option rather than a near-term solution to the Mundra smelter's concentrate requirements, noting the deal discloses no resource estimate, no production timeline, and no committed budget. The piece contends that India's copper supply security gap remains wide, and that the real signal is strategic intent rather than operational impact in the next 2-3 years.

headline: AUSTRALIAN MINES SCONI SCANDIUM: 27 METRES AT 883 PPM FROM SURFACE AT LUCKNOW — Old Drill Hole Review Unlocks New Target
snippet: Australian Mines (ASX: AUZ) reported November 13 that a review of historical drill holes at its Sconi multi-metal project in Queensland identified 27 metres at 883 parts per million scandium from surface at the Lucknow zone — a grade and depth profile that supports the viability of a targeted new scandium drilling programme. Scandium's critical mineral designation and its use in solid oxide fuel cells and aluminum alloys has drawn fresh investor attention to the Sconi project beyond its nickel-cobalt resource, with the shallow high-grade intercept presenting a low-capex entry point for new exploration.
